To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) d rays play a dominant role in HZE induced neuron morphological changes, 2) the role of track-structure is important, 3) the effects of radiation quality and dose on neuron morphology are similar for low and high LET particles, and 4) the role of neuron cell death in the prediction of morphometric parameters must be considered.

we developed a biophysical model of heavy ion radiation induced morphological changes in mouse hippocampal granular cell layer neurons, which is based on stochastic track structure, and predicts important differences between 16O, 48Ti, 16O and d rays, due to the spatial distribution of damage.
we have used stochastic track structure calculations to develop a predictive biophysical model of HZE radiation-induced morphological changes to neuron dendritic arbor structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a predictive model for heavy ion radiation induced changes to the complex morphology of dendritic arbours in mouse hippocampal neurons.

the development of a predictive model of the effects of HZE particles on neuron morphology and the application of the model to elucidate the role and effects of track structure on morphological changes.
developing a biophysical model to predict the morphological changes to neurons that result from heavy ion exposure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stochastic distribution of damage sites is the most important factor in determining the morphological changes to neurons in mouse hippocampus GCL neurons.
the model predicts a significant reduction in the complexity of dendritic arbours for mouse dentate GCL neurons exposed to 48Ti and 16O ions at 600 MeV/u.

the stochastic nature of the distribution of damage sites in the dendritic arbor plays a key role in predicting morphometric parameters and that this stochastic distribution of sites is a function of the spatial distribution of ED by both primary ions and d rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stochastic distribution of d ray damage is the major factor in the dose and LET dependence of HZE particle induced neuron morphological changes, and the stochastic distribution of damage sites is an important factor for predicting morphometric changes in single neuron dendritic arbors.
the stochastic nature of ED and the spatial distribution of damage are key features of HZE induced neuron morphological changes.
a model of the stochastic nature of microscopic ED by d rays is necessary to accurately predict HZE particle induced morphological damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
d ray track structure plays a major role in the morphological changes of dendrites in mouse GCL neurons.
the stochastic nature of particle track structure is important for predictions of HZE particle induced morphological damage to dendrites and the resulting cognitive detriments.
a biophysics model of microscopic ED and its distribution can provide a quantitative framework to understand the role of particle track structure in the development of cognitive detriments.
